augmentation.proposed_attribute: Full Term Premium Original Whole Cover Currency Code
augmentation.note: I DISAGREE WITH THE BRIEF FRAMING OF THESE COLUMNS, on measured evidence. The brief calls the _SWF columns CURRENCY TWINS and warns that 'a currency twin and its base are DISTINCT values and must not share one attribute'. The anti-collapse half is right and is honoured. But they are almost certainly NOT a second AMOUNT: measured on 00_tables_index.json, all 9 _SWF columns are TEXT and all 9 of their paired bases are NUMBER, 9 for 9. A currency-CONVERTED amount would be numeric. A TEXT companion to a numeric amount is a qualifier - on an Oracle insurance core the overwhelmingly likely reading is the CURRENCY CODE the paired amount is expressed in. So each _SWF column is mapped as the currency qualifier OF ITS OWN amount, which keeps all 18 columns distinct (the brief requirement) without asserting nine phantom amounts. CONSEQUENCE IF I AM WRONG: the nine attributes are misnamed but still distinct and still one-per-source-column, so nothing is overwritten and the fix is a rename, not a re-key. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: two sample values of any one _SWF column - routed to SOURCE. The expansion of SWF itself is unverified. NOT mapped to SAT_POLICY_HEADER 'Currency Code': that is ONE single-active attribute and nine columns writing it is a nine-way collapse (anti-collapse rule 1); and these are per-amount qualifiers, not the policy currency.
augmentation.child_key_note: both declared legs are real value columns on this view, so the coverage row is named by the source itself; every other column on the pair is PAYLOAD on that one row. Precedent label reused verbatim.

columns.rationale: Discount percentage for the FAB section. THE SECOND ANTI-COLLAPSE DECISION OF THIS TABLE, and the hazard the brief routed here. FAB/FAC/BRC/BRJ x CD/LOAD x PER/AMT/YN is a 24-column repeating grid: FOUR package sections (FAB = fire/building, FAC = fire/contents, BRC = burglary/contents, BRJ = burglary/jewellery - read by Stage 3 against the SEC2_* premium columns on this same table) x TWO senses (CD = discount, LOAD = loading) = EIGHT discount/loading ITEMS, each with THREE attributes (a percentage, an amount and an applicability flag). It maps to the MULTI-ACTIVE SAT_POLICY_DISCOUNT_LOADING_APPLIED as EIGHT rows of three attributes - never 24 writers of one attribute, and never one row per column. CHILD KEY FOR STAGE 6, and this is the part that must be got right: Item Code must carry BOTH the section AND the discount/loading sense - FAB_CD, FAB_LOAD, FAC_CD, FAC_LOAD, BRC_CD, BRC_LOAD, BRJ_CD, BRJ_LOAD - because an Item Code of just 'FAB' collapses the discount onto the loading, and an Item Code of 'CD' collapses all four sections. The PER/AMT/YN triple are three ATTRIBUTES of one row, NOT three child-key values (Stage 3 said this explicitly). The estate vocabulary for this satellite is the OPUS NAMED-LEG form - opus writes 'Item Code = COMMERCIAL_DISC' where base wrote bare labels such as 'Family Discount' - and the brief rules that opus governs, so Stage 6 must use 'Item Code = FAB_CD' and not a bare token. The section-code expansion is a naming inference with no sample data behind it; the GRID STRUCTURE, however, is certain from the column names alone. TYPE ODDITY, measured: the four *_CD_PER columns are TEXT while the four *_LOAD_PER columns are NUMBER, so the discount percentages are stored as text in this feed - a cast is needed and a non-numeric value is possible.

Precedent already writes scoped head codes to this satellite ('Tax Head Code = SERVICE_TAX', '= S_TAX'), so the form is estate-established.

columns.rationale: TP finance type - an EXACT existing attribute name on the external third-party link satellite. THIS IS THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE FOR THE TP READING: the model carries 'TP Finance Type' in a satellite whose other attributes are TP Insurer Name, TP Policy Number and TP Tenure Years, i.e. third-party motor cover, and this source has a column that lands on it exactly. A tie-up-partner reading explains none of that. TP / BTP AMBIGUITY - RESOLVED FOR THE CHILD KEY BY NOT RESOLVING IT, which is the point. Stage 3 deliberately left TP_ open between THIRD PARTY (the Motor sense) and TIE-UP PARTNER, tagged both readings across 36 columns, and told Stage 4 to pick one and say so. My reading is THIRD PARTY, on evidence from the MODEL rather than from the column name: data_7.js itself uses TP to mean third party in SAT_POLICY_EXTERNAL_TP_LINK (TP Insurer Name, TP Policy Number, TP Tenure Years, TP Finance Type) and SAT_POLICY_TP_PRIOR_PERIOD, and BJAZ_POLICY_BASES_EXTN carries a TP_FIN_TYPE column that lands exactly on the existing 'TP Finance Type' attribute - a coincidence the partner reading does not explain. BTP then reads as BASIC third party, the standard Indian motor pairing. AGAINST: PARTNER_GSTN sits in the same tax block on both twins, which is what made Stage 3 hesitate; it is explained independently as the GSTIN of the distribution partner, which belongs in any tax block. NOT PRESENTED AS SETTLED - no sample data exists and this is a naming inference. CRITICALLY, THE DECISION COSTS NOTHING IF IT IS WRONG: the child-key values below use the SOURCE OWN TOKENS verbatim (TP_CGST, BTP_ADJ_SGST ...) rather than an interpreted word, which is the convention opus_health34 ratified for its 12 GPA benefit heads. So being wrong about the expansion of TP renames nothing and re-keys nothing; only the prose above would change.
